questions.question: An iterative method has a rule for moving from the current solution to a new one. What is the role of its stopping condition?
options: It specifies how the next solution is computed from the current one
It specifies the solution from which the method has to start
It specifies when the required answer has actually been obtained
It specifies how fast each iteration of the method must run

questions.question: The problem $\min\{x^2+bx+c\colon x\ge d\}$ has the optimum $x^*=\max\{-b/2,d\}$. Why is no iterative algorithm needed to solve it?
options: It has only one constraint, and one constraint needs no iterations
Iterations are needed only when the objective is linear
A closed-form answer exists: the data give $x^*$ directly
Problems with a single variable never need an algorithm

questions.question: A warehouse holds 50 units. In each iteration it ships 12 units, provided at least 12 units are in stock; it stops as soon as fewer than 12 units remain. How many units remain at the end?
options: 2 units
14 units
4 units
38 units

questions.question: Which of these tasks can be answered by a direct formula, with no repeated iterations needed?
options: Finding the shortest visiting order of 30 towns
Finding a timetable for 200 lectures in 40 rooms
Finding a packing of 500 boxes into few lorries
Finding the $x\ge0$ that makes $x^2-8x$ smallest

questions.question: An optimization method for a cost-minimization model produces, in some iteration, a plan with lower cost than any found so far, but the plan violates one of the model's constraints. How should the method treat it?
options: As the new best plan, since lower cost is the goal
Not as an acceptable answer, however low its cost
As the final answer, since no lower cost was found
As acceptable if it violates only one constraint

questions.question: Projects A (cost 4, value 10), B (cost 5, value 11) and C (cost 6, value 12) compete for a budget of 10. A rule repeatedly adds the remaining project with the highest value per unit cost that still fits, and stops when none fits. Which total value does it return?
options: 21, which is the best value possible
22, by choosing projects A and C
33, by choosing all three projects
21, though 22 fits within the budget
